tasks.objective: Scaffold the frontend application (TypeScript + React 18 + Vite) and implement the canonical Workflow Definition JSON Schema module plus a pure graph validator that enforces the approved schema (required fields, node/edge integrity, no cycles, start/end reachability).

acceptance_tests.method: Run `npm ci && npm run typecheck` in frontend/.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Dependencies install and TypeScript compiles with zero errors.

acceptance_tests.method: Run `npm run test -- --run src/workflow/validateGraph.test.ts` (Vitest) covering a valid multi-node DAG and invalid fixtures.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Valid fixture passes; fixtures with a cycle, missing 'start', no 'end', dangling edge endpoint, duplicate node id, and an agent node missing agent_definition_id/model_profile_id/tool_policy_id are each rejected with a path-specific error.

acceptance_tests.method: Validate workflow.schema.json against the JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 meta-schema using ajv compile.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Schema compiles with ajv 8 in strict mode without errors; schema_version is a required const '1.0'.

tasks.objective: Implement the drag-and-drop canvas editor: React Flow surface with pan/zoom, a node-type palette for all 11 approved node types, node add/move/delete, and edge creation/selection backed by a Zustand store holding the canonical workflow document.

acceptance_tests.method: Run `npm run test -- --run src/editor/WorkflowCanvas.test.tsx` (@testing-library/react + jsdom, React Flow mocked where needed).
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Dropping an 'agent' palette item adds exactly one agent node to the store; connecting two node handles creates one edge with correct source_node_id/target_node_id; deleting a node removes its incident edges.

acceptance_tests.method: Start dev server (`npm run dev`) and add/move/connect nodes in the browser.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: All 11 node types (start, agent, condition, gate, parallel, join, human_approval, tool, memory, delay, end) are placeable; canvas pans and zooms; nodes are draggable and edges render.

tasks.objective: Implement the property panels: a node inspector that configures each node type's config (agent definition, model profile, tool policy for agent nodes; contract/gate type for gate nodes; tool name/params, condition expression, delay, memory scope), and an edge inspector for output_mapping, condition, on_error and max_retries, with the validator's errors surfaced inline per field.

acceptance_tests.expected_result: Selecting an agent node renders selectors for agent definition, model profile and tool policy sourced from the API client; editing fields updates the store node config; missing required config triggers a field-level validation error message.
Selecting an edge exposes output_mapping, condition, on_error (fail|retry|skip) and max_retries controls, and changes persist into the edge object.

tasks.objective: Implement the typed persistence API client against the approved REST contract plus JSON export/import and version save. Client covers workflow definition CRUD, version listing/snapshot, and reference list endpoints, with an in-memory mock adapter for offline development and a real HTTP adapter, using RFC 9457 error handling.

acceptance_tests.method: Run `npm run test -- --run src/api/client.test.ts src/editor/importExport.test.ts` with fetch mocked.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: create/update/get/list/versions operations issue the correct method, URL and body per the contract; a 422 Problem Details response is surfaced as a typed error; export produces a JSON blob validating against workflow.schema.json; import round-trips a valid file and rejects a malformed one without mutating the store.

acceptance_tests.method: Integration check against the orchestration server (t_52732c01) once /api/v1/workflows/definitions is available, otherwise record as pending-deferred in the task handoff.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Saving a definition then re-fetching it returns the identical definition JSON and increments/persists a WorkflowVersion snapshot; if the endpoint is unavailable, the mock adapter path is demonstrated end-to-end instead.

tasks.objective: Author and run the unit/component test suite for the core editor modules (validator, store, canvas, property panels, api client, import/export) and wire the `make check` gate so it runs install, typecheck, lint, unit tests, schema validation and build.

acceptance_tests.expected_result: The command executes `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test -- --run`, schema validation, and `npm run build`, and exits 0 with all checks passing.

acceptance_tests.method: Inspect coverage report for core modules.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Line coverage for src/workflow and src/editor is >= 80%, and the suite fails on any unhandled TypeScript or ESLint error.

tasks.objective: Author and run end-to-end tests with Playwright covering the simple workflow creation flow: open editor, drag an agent node plus start/end nodes, connect them, configure the agent node's agent/model/tool policy, save, and reload to confirm persistence; verify import/export and cycle rejection.

acceptance_tests.method: Run `npx playwright test e2e/workflow-creation.spec.ts` against the built app with the mock adapter.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: The scenario builds start->agent->end, configures the agent node, saves, reloads the page and observes the same graph; the produced definition passes validateGraph with zero errors.

acceptance_tests.method: Add an e2e case that attempts to close a cycle and one that imports the fixture.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: The cycle attempt is blocked with a visible validation error; importing valid-workflow.json renders the expected nodes/edges.

tasks.objective: Independently review the implemented editor against the acceptance criteria (usable editor producing valid workflow JSON, passing validation, storing/retrieving definitions), the approved architecture interfaces, and security expectations (no secrets in exported JSON, tool-policy fields are configuration-only).

acceptance_tests.method: Reviewer re-runs `make check` and the Playwright suite from a clean checkout and inspects the diff.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: All tests pass independently; no fabricated evidence; findings are documented with file/line references.

acceptance_tests.method: Inspect exported/imported JSON and the schema for credential leakage.
acceptance_tests.expected_result: Exported definitions contain only references (agent_definition_id, model_profile_id, tool_policy_id) and no provider secrets or tokens; tool policy represented as configuration data, not enforcement.

definition_of_done: All tasks TASK-001 through TASK-007 are completed with their acceptance tests executed and evidence recorded.
A user can visually assemble, configure, save, reload and export/import a multi-agent workflow through the editor UI.

Every produced or imported workflow definition validates against workflow.schema.json (Draft 2020-12) and the graph validator (single start node, at least one end, no cycles, reachable nodes, required agent references).
Definitions persist through the approved REST contract (/api/v1/workflows/definitions, .../versions) and are retrieved identically; version snapshots are created on save.
`make check` runs the mandatory test/lint/typecheck/schema/build gate and exits 0 (AC-14).
Playwright end-to-end coverage demonstrates the simple workflow creation flow and reload persistence.
No approved architectural decisions (PostgreSQL/JSONB domain model, Workflow Definition JSON Schema interface, OpenAPI 3.0 contract) were silently changed.
No provider secrets or credentials appear in exported workflow JSON or in the repository.
Unit coverage for src/workflow and src/editor is >= 80%.
Reviewer evidence is linked to the produced artifact and open findings are either resolved or explicitly deferred.
rollback_notes: The frontend is a greenfield directory (frontend/); reverting the feature is a removal of that directory plus its build config and does not affect the backend or database.
No database migration or destructive operation is introduced by this task; schema persistence lives behind the REST API owned by the orchestration server (t_52732c01).

The editor is pinned to workflow schema_version '1.0'; if the schema changes, forward-compatible migration logic must live in WorkflowService, not in the editor, so the editor can be reverted independently.
Persistence uses the versioned /api/v1 path; a revert to a prior editor build keeps working against the same API version as long as only additive changes are made.
Do not delete the shared frontend directory while TASK-002..TASK-007 depend on it; roll back only after all dependent tasks are complete or reverted in reverse dependency order.
